# Sparse diagonal stroke continuation

## When to use
Use when an ARC grid has a mostly uniform background and compact sparse motifs that may encode diagonal lines extended to grid boundaries. This is a class-level hypothesis workflow, not an ID-specific answer recipe.

## Workflow
1. Record all non-background coordinates and group by color. Separate same-color aligned pairs/segments from isolated cells and from mixed-color diagonal chains.
2. For each plausible same-color segment, test both diagonal orientations (down-right/up-left and down-left/up-right). Identify segment endpoints and compute exact ray cells to boundaries without altering the seed.
3. Compare each prediction against every demo output. Record which colors/segments extend, which directions fire, and which plausible near-matches are unchanged. Do not infer that every diagonal pair activates.
4. Apply only the demonstrated selector and ray paths to the test. Preserve other cells and seed colors unless outputs explicitly change them. Mechanically validate dimensions and coordinate indices.
5. After incorrect feedback, reject that hypothesis and identify the alternative selector distinction; do not repeat a similar output with minor transcription changes.

## Pitfalls
- Mixed-color objects can resemble a diagonal run; require same-color evidence unless demos show otherwise.
- Extending all same-color diagonal segments is not established merely because one demo extends a pair. A test submission extending both a 9 diagonal pair and a separate 1 pair was rejected. Selector behavior was not fully revealed.
- Examples show variable direction and palette: a color-6 diagonal seed extended up-left to the top boundary, a color-7 seed extended down-left to the bottom, and a color-9 pair extended down-left. Derive direction per instance.
- Stroke endpoints may already contain multiple seed cells; preserve every original seed cell and extend outward from the correct endpoint rather than overwriting or filling the whole diagonal indiscriminately.

## Evidence scope
Task-4fbd50f1 supplied three demos and two incorrect test submissions.
